subject: Polaris rollout - SRE capacity constraints updated
body:

Following up on yesterday's platform sync. The SRE team has finalized their capacity assessment for Polaris rollout monitoring.

subject: Auth endpoint migration - analytics-worker refactor taking longer than expected
body:
Jorge,

Quick update on the legacy auth endpoint migration. We hit a snag with analytics-worker - turns out there are 14 hard-coded endpoint references scattered across the codebase, not the 5-6 we initially scoped. My team has refactored 8 so far, but the remaining 6 are in some gnarly async batch processing logic.

Revised estimate: we'll need until EOD April 11 to complete analytics-worker + reporting-batch (which depends on it). That's +3 days from our original April 8 target.

The good news: legacy-webhook-proxy only handles 0.3% of auth traffic (mostly old integrations from 2023). I propose we deprioritize it and migrate those last few customers manually if needed. That would let us hit the April 11 completion date with higher confidence.

Health checks for the already-migrated services (user-service, api-gateway, mobile-backend) are all green - no regressions.

Let me know if the +3 day slip creates issues for your customer notification timeline. I can pull in another engineer if we absolutely need to hit April 8, but it'll cost us velocity on Polaris.

Priya

subject: Re: Auth endpoint migration - checkpoint decision needed
body:

Thanks for the heads-up. The +3 day slip is manageable - it pushes our Go/No-Go checkpoint from April 10 to April 11, which still gives us a 30-day customer grace period if we send notification on April 14 (accounting for legal review).

I agree with deprioritizing legacy-webhook-proxy. Let's document which customers are affected and have a manual migration plan ready.

Marcus - can you confirm SRE capacity for health checks and monitoring on April 11? We need sign-off that all migrated services are stable before we commit to customer notification.

I'm drafting the customer communication in parallel (migration guide, FAQ, support scripts) so we're ready to move fast once engineering gives the green light. If we slip beyond April 11, we'll need to either compress the grace period to 21 days (contractual minimum) or push the kill-switch date to late May, which conflicts with Q2 planning.

Jorge

body:
